report:
## Conclusion

**The claim is well-supported by high-quality evidence.** Exemestane (25 mg/day), an oral steroidal aromatase inhibitor, significantly reduces breast cancer incidence in postmenopausal women at elevated risk.

### Key Evidence

The primary evidence comes from the **MAP.3 (Mammary Prevention 3) trial**, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III study published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* in 2011 (Goss et al.). The trial enrolled **4,560 postmenopausal women** at increased risk for breast cancer. Exemestane reduced the incidence of **invasive breast cancer by 65%** compared to placebo over a median follow-up of about 3 years. The reduction was primarily in estrogen receptor–positive tumors.

**ASCO clinical practice guidelines** subsequently recommended exemestane as one of several options (alongside tamoxifen, raloxifene, and anastrozole) for breast cancer risk reduction in postmenopausal women at increased risk, strengthening earlier, more tentative recommendations.

### Caveats

- **Side effects**: Exemestane was associated with declines in bone mineral density and menopausal symptoms (hot flashes, joint pain), though side effects were generally described as mild to moderate.
- **Uptake remains low** in clinical practice despite guideline endorsement, likely due to side-effect concerns and patient/provider preferences.
- Long-term data on durable cancer reduction in the prevention setting are still limited compared to the treatment setting.

### Sources

1. Goss PE et al., "Exemestane for Breast-Cancer Prevention in Postmenopausal Women," *NEJM*, 2011 — https://www.nejm.org/doi/suppl/10.1056/NEJMoa1103507/suppl_file/nejmoa1103507_appendix.pdf
2. ASCO 2011 coverage of MAP.3 results — https://ecancer.org/en/news/1790-asco-2011-exemestane-significantly-reduces-risk-of-invasive-breast-cancer-in-high-risk-postmenopausal-women
3. ASCO clinical practice guideline on endocrine therapy for breast cancer risk reduction — https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.19.01461
4. Long-term efficacy and safety review of exemestane — https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/10.2147/PPA.S42223
